title: Artifacts render as content
revisionReason: Both blocking findings from the second review are fixed ('self' removed from the policy; the e2e spec now observes the app's own origin). The caption was replaced with a modest one on a founder ruling, and a simplification pass cut the escape backstop, seven probes and three spelling assertions. All gates green; PR open.

phases: build in one session: tests then code — DONE
fresh-agent review — ran three rounds; all blocking findings fixed

artifacts.prunedOnReview: Seven one-off scripts (probe.mjs, p2.cjs, li-probe.cjs, height-probe.cjs, browser-frame-probe.cjs, inherited-assumptions-probe.cjs and their results) and seven screenshots. The durable browser proof is the e2e specs, which run against the shipped code rather than a bespoke harness. See round.md §12.

rendering: lsof -nP -iTCP:5179 -sTCP:LISTEN   # must be empty before you believe anything below
cd layers/core-ui && CI=1 npx playwright test __e2e__/AZ6-artifact-frame.spec.ts __e2e__/AZ6-artifact-content.spec.ts
howToReproduce.note: No server or database needed. The e2e specs mock the artifact API at the network layer and drive the real production components; the isolation probes serve their own host page plus two listeners — one third-party and one standing in for the app's own origin. CI=1 turns off Playwright's reuseExistingServer, which is what stops a sibling worktree's stale server answering silently.

measuredFacts.environment: Electron 43.1.1 / Chromium 150.0.7871.114 (the version applications/desktop pins); plus Chromium 149 via Playwright for the web form factor
measuredFacts.preloadBridgeInIframes: ABSENT in all frames including an un-sandboxed same-origin one — window.__HYPERIDLE__ (api key + credential IPC) is main-frame only
measuredFacts.sandboxAllowScriptsOnly: script runs; origin null; parent DOM / cookies / localStorage / same-origin API all blocked
measuredFacts.sandboxPlusAllowSameOrigin: full parent DOM read, localStorage, and successful call to the app's own API — the documented escape, confirmed
measuredFacts.exfiltrationWithoutCsp: a sandboxed frame with no CSP reached an outside server by fetch AND by image beacon — sandbox alone does not stop network
measuredFacts.selfResolvesToTheAppOrigin: in a srcdoc document Chromium resolves CSP 'self' against the opaque origin's PRECURSOR — the embedding app's origin. Every 'self' was a grant to HyperIdle itself, opening eight channels. All removed; the policy now grants no origin at all.
measuredFacts.frameSrcPinsTheArtifact: egress-matrix-result.json row C — loosening only the INNER policy changes nothing; it is the SHELL's frame-src 'none' that stops self-navigation. That is why there are two layers.
measuredFacts.webrtcDirectiveIsDead: Chromium logs 'Unrecognized Content-Security-Policy directive webrtc'. With the directive set but the constructor neutraliser removed, 4 UDP packets left the frame. The neutraliser is what closes it.
measuredFacts.desktopWebPreferences: main.ts:529-535 and 634-641 — contextIsolation true, sandbox true; nodeIntegration / nodeIntegrationInSubFrames / webviewTag unset (safe defaults); webSecurity on
measuredFacts.appCsp: none anywhere in the repo today; a srcdoc frame would inherit one if added later

decisionByKind.rawHtmlInsideTextBody: DOMPurify default profile, inline, no scripts — same policy as Knowledge
decisionByKind.html: its own document in a NESTED iframe inside a shell we compose, both sandbox="allow-scripts" exactly, both carrying the policy; scripts and styles run

enforcement: The sandbox string and the policy live in one srcdoc builder. ArtifactFrame takes only { html, title? } — there is no prop by which a call site can loosen either. Component tests assert the rendered sandbox attribute and the exact policy string; because the e2e lane is local-only, those constant assertions are the only CI-visible guard against a host or 'self' going back into the policy.
gapNotDesignedAround: No separate serving origin for artifacts exists. Not needed for this decision (the opaque origin does the isolating, measured), but it is what a future artifact needing localStorage, ES modules or declared network access would require — and it is also the door to being a real MCP Apps host. Its own work package.
nextAction: PR open against main; wait for CI. Do not merge.
constraints: No change to how artifacts are produced or stored.
No new design-system component whose job an existing export already does (ArtifactFrame is new because no export renders a sealed document).
Out of scope: separate serving origin, app-wide CSP, artifact-to-app message bridge, page anatomy (AZ11), artifact lists (AZ9), editing.

reviewFixes.round1 self-navigation: Two-layer shell: the artifact is a NESTED frame inside a shell we compose, whose policy carries frame-src 'none'. Measured single-layer the self-nav reached a listener; two-layer it is ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CSP.
reviewFixes.round1 WebRTC: webrtc 'block' is NOT enforced in this Chromium (measured: directive set, packets still left). The constructors are removed from the artifact document before its script runs, non-writable/non-configurable, with no borrowable realm.
reviewFixes.round1 blind seal spec: Every channel asserted BY NAME plus a real UDP listener. Also fixed a trap inside the fix: the listener recorded '/NAME' while assertions compared 'NAME', making every per-channel check unfalsifiable.
reviewFixes.round1 unrenderable state lied: isRegisteredKind now separates unknown-kind / empty / malformed, one sentence each, no source control when there is nothing to reveal.
reviewFixes.round2 'self' is not 'none': Every 'self' removed from the policy. The artifact reaches no origin at all — inline script and style, data: for its own assets, nothing else.
reviewFixes.round2 the spec was blind to it: A same-origin observer via route interception (which sits downstream of the policy check, so a handler that runs means the request genuinely left). Twelve channels asserted by name.
reviewFixes.round3 the caption promised an absolute: Replaced on a founder ruling with a line that says what the frame IS rather than enumerating what it cannot do. Nothing escapes is impossible in IT, and this is an MVP.

simplificationCuts.escapeBackstop: DELETED — guarded a case nothing in an artifact can reach, and the Open larger dialog rendered the identical srcDoc with no counter, so it could not have been load-bearing. frame-src 'none' is what holds. Lore explaining why no backstop is needed was kept.
simplificationCuts.probes: PRUNED to the four that carry a claim nothing else does, plus the before/after outcome pair.
simplificationCuts.spellingAssertions: Three deleted (configurable:false, e.source!==f.contentWindow, and a constant asserted against its own definition). The describe('the policy') block was deliberately left — it is the only CI-visible guard on the policy string.
